item.description:
### Added - See the pages an Agent's web search found. Open a search in a chat to get its results as chips with each site's icon and page title; a chip opens the page. Codex and Claude searches both show their pages, live and when you come back to a chat. - Google Antigravity is a built-in Agent with its own section in **Settings > Agents**. It starts with a profile that uses the account `agy` is signed in to on your computer, so an `agy` you already use works with no setup. Add a profile for each other account and sign in with Google or connect a Gemini API key, Gemini Enterprise or Agent Platform. Nodex downloads and updates the Antigravity runtime for you, or runs the `agy` you point it at. Chats use the models on your plan with each model's thinking levels, list what Antigravity's subagents did, and its limits sit beside your other usage meters. - Antigravity conversations, from the Antigravity app or its `agy` command line, can be imported from **Settings > Import** beside Codex and Claude Code. They appear in the same list across every folder, with search, filters and batch import. Each import is a new chat that already shows the full history, including thoughts, commands, file edits and tool calls, and continues as your Antigravity profile. The original conversation stays unchanged. - Choose which large parts of Nodex stay on your Mac. **Settings > General > Add-ons** lists the parts that install after the app, with a switch to remove each one and get its space back: Desktop Tools (the Browser, your Chrome tabs and Computer Use for Agents), Codex, Claude Code (for Claude with an API key or Nodex credits) and Document Tools (Word, PowerPoint, Excel and PDF files for Agents). - Run your own Codex. **Settings > Agents > Codex > Codex executable** takes a command or path, and Nodex runs that Codex instead of its own. Nodex shows its version and warns when it differs from the one Nodex is tested with; Desktop Tools stay off in Codex chats while you use it. - The Subagents tab opens on a map of how a chat's work was delegated. The lead sits on one side and each subagent is a card naming its Agent, model and effort. Each edge takes the color of the harness the work went to and shows whether that work is under way, waiting on you, or back. Subagents that delegate further appear beneath their own card, at any depth. A switch at the top returns to the list. - Decide whether subagents can hand work to more Agents. **Settings > Chats > Let subagents delegate** sets it for every chat, and the Subagents tab can answer differently for one chat. When it is off, only the Agent you talk to delegates or starts new chats; you can also just ask that Agent to keep a task to itself. Subagents now work on their own task first and delegate only when the task calls for it. - Your agents work together from the first chat. When setup finds two different agents ready, such as Codex and Claude Code, it says so, and the first task asks one to bring in the other by name: they study your project independently and compare notes, or one builds and the other reviews. You watch the second agent at work in the same chat. Asking for an agent by name works in any chat afterwards. - Nodex introduces things as you meet them. The first time an agent writes a Page, another agent could give a second opinion, or you start a chat while one is still working, one quiet sentence above the Composer says what it is and offers a way to try it, such as `Ask Claude Code` or `Open Inbox`. Each tip appears once and leaves when you act on it, dismiss it or send your next message. **Settings > General > Show tips** turns them off. - Reach the people who make Nodex from inside the app. **Feedback & community** in the account menu at the bottom of the rail opens the Nodex Discord server, or copies the number of the Nodex QQ group so you can find it in QQ. Bring bug reports, ideas and questions. - Codex replies that OpenAI's safeguards hide or block after they stream now stay hidden. Nodex shows a short notice in their place, on your phone too, and other Agents reading the chat see the notice instead of the reply. A reply shown with a support note keeps that note beneath it.
### Changed - Settings is easier to find your way around. The sidebar now groups pages by what they are about — the App, your Agents, Integrations, Coding and Data — and every page says what it controls. **Chats** gathers what chats may do without asking, your instructions and how chats look; **Editor** gathers typing, pasting and links; Hooks moved into **Plugins** and Environments into **Worktrees**. **Spaces** is now **Remote**, where you link your phone, invite people and join other computers, and Link a device turns remote connections on for you. Conversations is now **Import**, and Data controls is **Archived chats**. - Each Agent's models are now in its own card in **Settings > Agents**, beside how it signs in, with Nodex's credit-spending models first. A filter at the top finds any model across them. Only Nodex keeps a switch for all of its models; turn another Agent or profile off to turn all of it off. - Branches Nodex creates for chats now start with `nodex/` instead of `codex/`. A prefix you set in **Settings > Git** stays as it is. - A busy computer no longer puts "Agent execution isn't responding" on every window. Running many Agents, builds and tests at once now only slows Agent execution, and a chat that is still opening says your computer is busy and opens when Nodex catches up. The notice and its Restart appear only when Agent execution has made no progress for a minute. Opening a chat also goes ahead of background work and no longer waits while other Agents save their progress. - Nodex uses less memory and CPU while Agents work. When a chat changes, search now rereads only that chat instead of every chat, which on a Profile with thousands of chats removes about a gigabyte of short-lived memory a minute. Nodex's processes also hold about 75 MB less code and data for as long as they run, and a minimized or covered window stops redrawing until you show it. - Typing no longer waits on your disk. Drafts and other window state used to be rewritten and synced to disk with every keystroke, so a disk kept busy by builds and tests could hold up every window; they are now saved in the background, with changes made meanwhile saved together. - Opening many Pages no longer keeps them all in memory. A window keeps the four Pages you viewed most recently ready to show, and a Page older than that loads again when you return to its tab, with its undo history starting fresh. - A New tab is now a calm launcher: a search field for Pages, tools and websites, then the tools you pinned under Open. Pin, unpin and reorder tools from Open's … menu or with Customize, and every New tab in that panel follows your choice. Browser controls appear once the tab loads a site. - Setup lists the Agents that are ready first, then the ones already on your computer that need one more step, then the rest. A row keeps its place once it has one. - Antigravity has one place in Nodex: **Settings > Agents > Antigravity**. An Antigravity you connected under **Other agents** becomes its profile that uses `agy`'s sign-in on your computer, and its chats continue there once you choose an Antigravity model. Searching the ACP Registry for Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode now leads to the built-in Agent instead of adding a second copy. - Nodex for Mac is less than a third of its size: the installer drops from about 600 MB to 180 MB and the app from 2.1 GB to 0.64 GB. Desktop Tools download in the background after Nodex starts and work as soon as they arrive, with no restart. Codex, Claude Code and Document Tools download the first time you use them; if you already use Codex in Nodex, it comes back by itself after you update. Updates are less than a third of the size too, and bring a new version of a part only when that part changed, fetching it before you restart. - Nodex opens and works without Codex. Pages, search, Git and every other Agent no longer depend on it, so a missing or damaged Codex no longer stops the app from starting. - Streaming replies and long chats take far less work. While a long answer streams, Nodex's processes exchange about 17 times less data, and about 90 times less during a long thought: a reply's text travels between them once instead of with every update, and nothing is re-sent when it has not changed. Each update touches only its own message, and a long chat keeps only the messages near what you are reading on screen. - Chats no longer keep their JavaScript processes running after you stop using them. A chat's JavaScript session now closes after 30 minutes without use and starts fresh with its next JavaScript call, so a Nodex left running no longer collects a set of background processes for every chat that ran JavaScript. - Nodex opens with much less code in the way. Its window appears once about 1.4 MB of the app has loaded instead of 9.9 MB, with the rest loading behind it, and each window loads about 8 MB less: Pages, Databases, the Browser, the drawing canvas, the Terminal, the code highlighter and other surfaces load only when you open them, and error reporting only when it is on. - Returning to a chat you just left shows it at once. Each window keeps the three chats it most recently showed up to date for a minute, so switching back reads nothing again, and opening a chat now takes half the requests it did. - Code in chats and documents no longer slows the window while it is colored. Its text appears at once and is colored in the background as it scrolls into view; while a reply streams a code block, the part already colored keeps its colors as new lines arrive. - Nodex opens straight onto your first view. The window used to step from the Nodex mark to a blank window, then to a sidebar beside an empty pane, before the view appeared; now the mark stays until the view is ready and dissolves into it in one step, or swaps at once with Reduce motion. - Process Manager no longer weighs on the app while it is open. Each refresh reads every process once, away from the windows' main work, however many chats have background processes, and CPU now shows the share used since the previous refresh. - Searching chats no longer holds up the rest of Nodex. Results are ranked in the background, so typing in Find stays smooth while replies stream, and an idle Nodex no longer rereads every Codex chat each second: it refreshes only the chats that changed or whose host reconnected. - One Writing model writes chat titles, commit messages and pull request descriptions. Choose it in **Settings > Chats**; it replaces the chat title model, and any Agent can do the writing. When your choice is unavailable, Nodex uses the Agent of the chat you are in, then another available Agent. - Setup's first task reads in plain words and in your display language. It no longer asks for a "Nodex Page" before you have seen one. - An Agent's work in a chat reads as one live line. While it works, the line names the tool that is running, and each new tool's words wipe in as the last ones fade, without cutting in mid-shimmer. Its icon animates while the tool runs and holds still between tools. Opened, the steps hang from a thin line at their full length instead of scrolling in a short box: each command shows the command itself, each edit its file and line counts.
### Fixed - Searching a Page no longer takes over your cursor. After `Cmd/Ctrl+F` or opening a Page from a search result, the matched words used to stay selected, so clicking elsewhere and typing could jump back and replace them. Find now only highlights matches: you can click and type anywhere while it stays open, and its highlights follow your edits without scrolling the Page. Pressing Escape hands the current match to the Page as your selection. - Menus keep up with the pointer. Moving across the rows of a menu opened from a Page, Inbox item or other panel tab used to stall each highlight for a moment, because every row the pointer crossed made the whole window redraw. Rows now highlight as soon as the pointer reaches them, and hovering a menu no longer adds Back steps or clears Forward. - Clicking the group beside a Project's or Inbox's Home tab makes that group active. It used to switch straight back to Home's group. - Claude Agent can use Nodex's tools again. Its current releases ask for them in a form Nodex did not answer, so Nodex's own tools, such as Pages and Desktop Tools, were missing from its chats. Nodex now hands its tools to Claude Agent the way it does to every other ACP Agent. - Claude Agent chats offer Claude's slash commands as soon as they open, and its work no longer lists "Unsupported ACP update" steps. Nodex now speaks the current Agent Client Protocol, so commands an Agent lists when a chat starts reach the `/` menu and its newer updates are understood. - Drafting a commit message or pull request description works again. The draft buttons in **Commit or push** and **Create pull request** failed on every attempt. - A chat waiting on a long delegated task no longer shows as stalled in the Inbox. Nodex used to count only the chat's own messages as progress, so a chat that handed work to another Agent for more than twenty minutes was marked "Stalled · needs you" while that Agent was still working. Progress anywhere in the delegated work now counts. - A signed-in Codex no longer shows as "Isn't ready" with nothing to do. Setup, the Composer and the model menu now say what happened: signed in but unable to connect, not answering in time, or unable to start, each with Check again. Nodex reads Codex's sign-in from your computer before it asks the network, so being offline never hides your account. Codex is ready in about a second instead of about nine, and turns ready by itself when the connection returns. - Agents installed on your computer are found however Nodex was opened. Claude Code, OpenCode and Google Antigravity are found when Nodex starts from the Dock or Finder, even if your shell's startup files are slow or fail, and an older copy earlier on your PATH no longer hides a working one. A version too old to connect is shown with the version it needs, in setup and in Settings → Agents.
